messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "last thursday i got to the bus station early because i was going to meet my sister at the north entrance, and i had not been there in a long time. i thought the signs would make it straightforward, but the first one i saw had arrows for platforms and exits together, and i wasn't sure which arrow went with which words. i walked toward platform 6, then noticed that the number on the pillar was for the bay, not the platform, so i went back across the hall.

there was a map beside the ticket machines, although the small print was hard to read while people were standing in front of it. i asked a staff member where the north entrance was. she pointed toward a corridor and said, “keep going past the coffee shop, then turn left.” that was clearer than the signs, but i still checked the wall numbers as i walked. i arrived a few minutes before my sister. i felt a little foolish for getting turned around, though the station did have several signs that seemed to give different kinds of directions in the same place. i would probably leave extra time next time, even if i already knew the station better.", "output": "Last Thursday, I got to the bus station early because I was going to meet my sister at the north entrance, and I hadn’t been there in a long time. I thought the signs would make it straightforward, but the first one I saw had arrows for platforms and exits together, and I wasn’t sure which arrow went with which words. I walked toward platform 6, then noticed that the number on the pillar was for the bay, not the platform, so I went back across the hall.

There was a map beside the ticket machines, although the small print was hard to read with people standing in front of it. I asked a staff member where the north entrance was. She pointed toward a corridor and said, “Keep going past the coffee shop, then turn left.” That was clearer than the signs, but I still checked the wall numbers as I walked. I arrived a few minutes before my sister. I felt a little foolish for getting turned around, though the station did have several signs that seemed to give different kinds of directions in the same place. I’d probably leave extra time next time, even if I already knew the station better."}]
